Pattern: focal / patterned / diffuse
Family history of alopecia (ages, severity, sites)
Recent illness, surgery, pregnancy, weight loss (TE triggers)
items.detail: 3-month lag is classic for telogen effluvium.

items.label: Medications including new starts in last 3-6 months
Hair care practices: tension, heat, chemical processing
Symptoms: itch, burn, tenderness
items.detail: Symptomatic hair loss favors inflammatory cicatricial alopecia.

items.label: Systemic symptoms: thyroid, autoimmune, weight, energy
Pattern recognition: Norwood / Ludwig / Olsen
Hair pull test (50 hairs proximal-to-distal pull)
items.detail: Record number and scalp site. A healthy-volunteer study found ≤2 hairs in 97.2%; the historical >10% threshold is not a universal diagnostic cutoff.

items.label: Scalp inspection: erythema, scale, pustules, scarring, tufting
Trichoscopy (dermatoscope on scalp)
items.detail: Yellow dots (AGA), exclamation hairs (AA), peripilar casts (LPP), pinpoint white dots (FFA).

items.label: Eyebrows + body hair survey
Nail exam (pitting → AA, trachyonychia)
Select thyroid or iron studies when clinical assessment indicates; not a universal panel
CBC, CMP if systemic symptoms
Free testosterone + DHEA-S in F with patterned loss + virilization
ANA or syphilis testing only when the clinical differential warrants it
KOH + culture for tinea capitis if pediatric or scaly
4mm punch from active edge
items.detail: Avoid completely scarred areas — they lack diagnostic features.

items.label: Submit for BOTH vertical + horizontal sections
Separate DIF biopsy when indicated; agree site and transport medium with the receiving laboratory
items.detail: Do not assume saline is acceptable for routine transport. Local laboratory timing and handling requirements apply.

items.label: Indications: scarring, atypical pattern, refractory, dx uncertain
